subject: Next steps: deployment model and strict data segregation for Clearwood POC
messages:
From: Devon Collins <devon.collins@clearwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's architecture call — data custody & deployment questions

Thanks for the call earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams so we can line up the right internal stakeholders for the POC next week: 

1) Primary concern: we need firm confirmation on what stays in our VPC vs what touches Redwood-hosted control plane for both Dedicated and Private VPC options. Specifically: 
   - Where are raw request payloads stored (if at all)?
   - Are inference artifacts (logs/response cache) ever written to multi-tenant storage?
   - How are API keys / tokens handled?

2) Crypto & keys: we prefer customer-managed KMS if we move to Private VPC. If Dedicated is used, can we BYOK for model-serving keys or at least guarantee no keys leave our HSM?

3) Audit/logging: procurement wants a sample retention policy and an example audit log extract. Also need to confirm the level of access our auditors will get.

4) Timeline & cost: legal/procurement want a rough estimate of deployment lead time and a ballpark delta between Dedicated and Private VPC. If Private requires firewall/VPN peering setup, we need to budget engineering windows.

Attaching the POC mutual-action plan and a rough network diagram. Please mark up the MA plan with any follow-up items.

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Devon Collins <devon.collins@clearwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 17:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's architecture call — data custody & deployment questions

Hi Devon — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next step list so your teams can decide who to loop in: 

Short answers up front:
- Dedicated capacity: provides a dedicated tenant (isolated GPU pools and customer-specific storage for runtime artifacts). Requests are processed on infrastructure assigned to your tenant; we do not colocate customer inference state with other tenants.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): gives you a private control plane option and the ability to run the data plane inside your VPC. That path supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and fully private egress.

Important nuance: our hosted control plane (for Dedicated) does handle orchestration metadata (request ids, telemetry). We can minimize metadata retention and provide strict RBAC/audit controls — but if Clearwood requires zero Redwood-hosted control-plane residency, Private VPC is the path we recommend.

What we need from you to scope precisely:
- Which of the items below are non-negotiable vs negotiable for the POC:
   * Zero control-plane metadata outside your VPC
   * Customer-managed KMS for inference keys
   * Audit export to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch format)
   * No multi-tenant cache writes

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive (30m) w/ Marcus (solutions) + your infra lead to walk the network diagram and KMS options — can you propose windows next Tue/Wed?
2) We will produce a short appendix clarifying retention behavior and sample audit extracts (will attach SOC2 snapshot and one-pager).
3) If procurement/finance needs an initial cost delta, we can provide a ballpark within 48 hours after the tech deep-dive.

I attached a short POC checklist that highlights the differentiators — please review and flag the non-negotiables so we can prepare a tailored runbook.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood_PrivateVPC_one-pager.pdf (PDF, 140KB)]

From: Devon Collins <devon.collins@clearwood.com>

Date: Sun, 16 Mar 2025 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's architecture call — data custody & deployment questions

Thanks Olga. Helpful summary — we are leaning toward Private VPC for the POC because legal is insisting on control-plane residency and customer-managed keys for any PHI-adjacent workloads. A few clarifications before we schedule the deep-dive: 

- Can you provide the SOC2 evidence snapshot you mentioned (even redacted)? Procurement will want to confirm scope.
- What specifically is the required network configuration for Private VPC (peering + IP ranges + outbound rules)? In particular, can the control plane avoid public IPs if we require strict egress through our firewall?
- For Dedicated: please confirm whether any cache/prefix artifacts are ever written to shared storage for performance reasons. We need a firm statement we can present to legal.

I've looped in Priya (procurement) who will own contractual questions and timing. If you can provide the SOC2 snapshot and the network checklist, we will get our infra and legal on the proposed deep-dive.

Regards,
Devon

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Devon Collins <devon.collins@clearwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's architecture call — data custody & deployment questions

Devon — hi, Marcus here (Solutions Engineering). I pulled together the answers below to the specific checklist items so you have something to show legal and procurement ahead of the deep-dive. High-level: Dedicated is strong for data-plane isolation and faster time-to-production; Private VPC is required if you cannot accept any Redwood-hosted control-plane residency or if you need BYOK/HSM for the control plane.

Answers to checklist items:
- Raw request payloads: For Dedicated, request payloads are processed on tenant-assigned machines and are not written to multi-tenant persistent stores. Short-lived in-memory traces and ephemeral cache (per-instance) are used; we persist minimal telemetry to a customer-specific store for billing/observability only when configured. For Private VPC, you control both runtime and persistence (we do not retain payloads).
- Inference artifacts & cache: Dedicated uses isolated storage buckets per tenant for persisted artifacts. We do not write inference artifacts to shared buckets. When configured for maximum isolation we can disable all non-essential caches and ensure no write-through to longer-term storage.
- API keys/tokens: Keys are stored encrypted at rest. Dedicated uses Redwood-managed KMS by default; we can enable BYOK for Dedicated in some cases (requires contract addendum). Private VPC supports customer-managed KMS/HSM end-to-end.
- Audit/logging & retention: We can export logs to your S3 bucket or push to CloudWatch/Datadog. Retention and export cadence are configurable; sample audit extracts are attached.
- Network requirements (Private VPC): we support AWS VPC peering and PrivateLink. Control plane components can be deployed without public IPs if peering is in place; egress goes over your network. Required details: CIDR ranges, peering owner account, and firewall rules for the control plane port range (we'll send a short checklist).

Estimated timelines and ballpark delta:
- Dedicated: contract signed -> provision -> POC baseline in ~2–4 weeks.
- Private VPC: contract + network approvals -> infra provisioning -> POC baseline in ~6–10 weeks (depends heavily on peering and approvals).
- Ballpark cost delta: Private VPC typically carries a fixed setup fee and higher monthly minimums due to private control plane hosting — we will provide a draft estimate post deep-dive.

Attachments included: SOC2 snapshot (redacted), a short Private VPC one-pager, and a sample audit extract. If helpful, I can join the tech deep-dive and walk the exact network diagram and KMS flow. Proposed slots: Tue 2025-03-18 09:00 or Wed 2025-03-19 14:00 PT.

Next actions for Clearwood: 
1) Confirm which of the non-negotiables (Olga's list) must be satisfied for the POC.
2) Share a preferred tech-deep-dive slot and list of attendees (infra, security, legal).
3) If you want an NDA/architectural disclosure, we'll route the DocuSign and attach the full architecture deck.

Thanks — happy to jump on the call.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
